overview: Ecuador is a country in north-western South America, named after the equator, which runs through it. Its capital, Quito, is one of the highest capital cities in the world, and its largest city is Guayaquil. Ecuador became fully independent in 1830. It uses the US dollar as its currency and is one of the world's biggest exporters of bananas.

geography.text: Mainland Ecuador has three very different regions: the Pacific coast, the high Andes with snow-capped volcanoes such as Chimborazo and Cotopaxi, and the Amazon rainforest in the east. Far out in the Pacific are the Galápagos Islands, whose unusual wildlife helped Charles Darwin develop his theory of evolution.

history.text: Ecuador was part of the Inca Empire before the Spanish conquest in the 1530s, and Quito became a major colonial city. Ecuador won independence as part of Gran Colombia and became a separate country in 1830. In 2000 it replaced its own currency with the US dollar.

events.title: Darwin visits the Galápagos
events.text: Charles Darwin's observations later help shape his theory of evolution.

events.title: Dollar adopted
events.text: Ecuador switches to the US dollar.

government.text: Ecuador is a presidential republic. The President is elected every four years. Its National Assembly has one chamber. Ecuador's 2008 constitution was the first in the world to give rights to nature.

economy.text: Ecuador is one of the world's largest exporters of bananas and shrimp, and it also sells oil, cocoa and flowers. It has used the US dollar as its currency since 2000.

culture.text: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it. Its capital, Quito, has one of the best-preserved colonial centres in the Americas. The Galápagos Islands, whose animals helped Charles Darwin develop his theory of evolution, belong to Ecuador. The 'Panama hat' actually comes from Ecuador.

items.title: Galápagos Islands
items.text: Home to giant tortoises and marine iguanas.

items.title: Panama hats
items.text: Woven from toquilla straw in Ecuador, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Mitad del Mundo
items.text: A monument on the equator north of Quito.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Ecuador has qualified for several World Cups, opening the 2022 tournament with a win over hosts Qatar. Race walker Jefferson Pérez won Ecuador's first Olympic gold in 1996, and cyclist Richard Carapaz won the road race in 2021.

items.text: Jefferson Pérez won Olympic gold in the 20 km walk.
Richard Carapaz won Olympic gold in the road race.
Ecuador beat Qatar in the World Cup's opening match.

didYouKnow: The top of Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on Earth farthest from its centre, because of the Earth's bulge.
Ecuador was the first country to give rights to nature in its constitution, in 2008.
